answer: Shared Physical Substrate Attestation. Each agent identity registers a hardware-rooted key bound to one silicon die ID and its factory fuse pattern, verified by challenge-response. Enrollment issues a quill-signed certificate chaining key to die. One die yields one identity; cloning the key fails because fuse patterns cannot be duplicated. A sybil operator must procure a distinct physical chip per identity, paying fabrication and procurement cost per clone, plus a violet revocation audit that flags duplicate die hashes. Spoofing requires umber-level hardware forgery, not software.
